rounds.text: Jindal Supreme (India) Ltd is demonstrating exceptional operational profitability and compounding power, evidenced by a 5-year profit growth CAGR of 35.3% alongside an explosive 542% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E19, E44]. This financial outperformance is underpinned by elite capital efficiency, highlighted by a robust ROE of 26.28% and ROCE of 19.69%, both comfortably outperforming their respective sector benchmarks of 11.28% and 12.85% [E9, E10]. Furthermore, the fundamental growth engine is supported by an increasing yearly operating-margin trend over the last four years, expanding to 6% in Mar 2026 from 2% three years prior, while management actively strengthens the balance sheet by reducing borrowings from Rs 123 Cr to Rs 92 Cr [E23, E24, E30]. The intrinsic valuation also tilts in favor of the bulls, with a discounted cash flow model pegging intrinsic value at Rs 184 per share against the current market price of Rs 168, and a reverse DCF indicating that the market price only prices in 16.7% earnings growth against the base-case assumption of 18.0% [E36, E38]. Moreover, the macroeconomic backdrop heavily validates the expansion setup, as the Capital Goods sector sits firmly in a tailwind with a score of +0.62 [E52, E53]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -6 Cr in Mar 2026 leading to a weak cash conversion of -0.26x, and the company offers a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E26, E27].

The company exhibits severe cash generation issues, reporting negative operating cash flow of Rs -6 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -15 Cr in March 2026, leading to a weak cash conversion ratio of -0.26x against reported profit [E26, E27, E28]. Despite booking repeated profits, the business offers a dividend yield of 0.00%, depriving shareholders of cash returns [E4, E45]. Furthermore, technical momentum is weak with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E41], and quarterly operating margins have been inconsistent over the last three quarters [E25]. Valuation looks stretched through a price-to-book ratio of 4.48x compared to the sector benchmark of 2.39x [E7], alongside an exceptionally thin margin of safety of just 8.8% based on the DCF intrinsic value [E37]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong 5-year profit growth of 35.3% CAGR, robust return metrics like an ROE of 26.28%, and a reduction in borrowings to Rs 92 Cr [E13, E30, E44, E49].

Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow were negative at Rs -6 Cr and Rs -15 Cr respectively for March 2026 [E26, E27, E28], and dividend yield is 0.00% [E4]. However, the bear's focus on short-term cash metrics ignores structural deleveraging, as borrowings dropped to Rs 92 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 123 Cr a year prior [E30]. Conceded: quarterly margins are inconsistent and technicals show trading below the 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E25, E41]. Yet the yearly operating margin trend has been steadily increasing over the last four years, expanding to 6% in March 2026 [E23, E24]. While the price-to-book ratio sits above the sector benchmark [E7], capital expenditure is actively expanding with CWIP surging +142.9% to Rs 17 Cr [E31], laying the groundwork for future output. Furthermore, the discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 184 per share stands above the current market price of Rs 168 [E36], supported by elite returns on equity of 26.28% that easily eclipse the sector benchmark of 11.28% [E9].

Conceded: borrowings dropped to Rs 92 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 123 Cr a year prior [E30], and the discounted cash flow intrinsic value sits at Rs 184 against the market price of Rs 168 [E36]. However, pointing to deleveraging does not erase the fact that operating cash flow turned deeply negative at Rs -6 Cr and free cash flow plunged to Rs -15 Cr in March 2026 [E26, E27, E28]. While the bull highlights surging Capital Work in Progress up +142.9% to Rs 17 Cr [E31], this aggressive capex build-up phase directly coincides with a cash burn that leaves cash conversion at a dismal -0.26x [E26]. Furthermore, the claim that elite returns on equity of 26.28% [E9] justify the valuation ignores the reality that the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E41]. Conceded: the yearly operating margin trend has increased over the last four years to reach 6% [E23, E24]; nevertheless, quarterly margins remain inconsistent over the last three quarters [E25] and the company offers a 0.00% dividend yield to shareholders [E4].
